# VOR adaptation in the cerebellar flocculus

## HCD

Mossy fibres from `VN` reach the granule cells and the Golgi cells; climbing fibres from `IO` and parallel fibres from `GC(granule)` converge on `PC(purkinje)`, which inhibits `FTN`.

## Hypotheses

| ID | Element | Claims | Basis | Premises | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| H1 | UC GC(granule) | role | functional-need | [Ito, 1982] | The FRG needs a context expansion stage. |
| H2 | UC IO | transmitter | homology | [Lisberger, 1994] | Olivary neurons are glutamatergic in the monkey. |
| H3 | UC GoC(golgi) | population | analogy | [Eccles, 1967] | Golgi cells are a distinct population in the cat. |
| H4 | VN -> IO [Lisberger, 1994] | direction | indirect | [Lisberger, 1994] | Activity is correlated; the direction is not stated. |
| H5 | GoC(golgi) -> GC(granule) [Eccles, 1967] | existence | homology | [Eccles, 1967] | Golgi-to-granule inhibition is shown in the cat. |

Hypothesis connections: 2 of 7 (29%); hypothesis UCs: 3 of 6 (50%); limit 50%.

## Limitations

Laterality of the vestibular input is simplified.

## FRG

The TLF is realized by context representation, error-driven learning and feedforward gain control.
